- licence/regulatory: USFDA-inspected facility supporting access to regulated markets — evidence: "following statutory/regulatory inspections were conducted... U.S. [...] Unit -1... No observations... enables access to the regulated US market and other highly regulated global markets."

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- The Company faces pricing and competitive pressures, particularly in certain key products; fluctuations in raw material prices, demand changes and increased competition may impact margins and profitability.
- Geopolitical developments and disruptions in key shipping routes may affect availability and cost of raw materials, freight and logistics services.
- Operating in a stringent regulatory environment, changes in requirements, delays in approvals, or adverse observations from regulatory inspections may impact product commercialisation and access to regulated markets.
- Growth strategy depends on new product development subject to validation timelines, regulatory requirements and market acceptance; delays may affect anticipated growth and financial performance.
- Delays in customer payments or deterioration in customer creditworthiness may affect cash flows and working capital.
- Mahi Drugs' performance depends on successful commercialisation and ramp-up of new products and achieving optimum capacity utilisation; delays or lower-than-optimal utilisation may pressure its financial performance.
- Sales pressure in the Ranitidine business, tied to a major customer's financial challenges, illustrates dependence on key products and product-specific market pressures.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Strengthening the core API and intermediates business while pursuing portfolio diversification.
- Expansion into regulated and international markets.
- Development and commercialisation of new products, including through strategic collaborations.
- Growth in contract manufacturing.
- Capacity optimisation and improved operational leverage.
- Strengthening customer relationships and reducing dependence on a limited number of products.
- Continued investment in R&D, process development and regulatory capabilities.
- Improving Mahi Drugs' (subsidiary) capacity utilisation and product commercialisation.
